title: Distributor Trade Claims and Scheme Settlement
summary: Read distributor claim sheets and proofs, apply scheme rules from your circulars, recalculate eligible amounts, catch duplicates and give finance a clean credit note sheet to approve.

seo.title: Distributor Trade Claims and Scheme Settlement | VipraTech
seo.description: AI checks distributor scheme, damage and display claims against invoices, proofs and circulars, recalculates amounts and flags duplicates for finance.

problem.intro: FMCG and packaged-food brands run many schemes through distributors at once: quantity slabs, free goods, retailer display payments, damage and expiry returns, rate differences, and transport or salesman reimbursements. Every month each distributor sends a claim sheet with supporting invoices and proofs, and a small team checks them before finance issues credit notes.

pain_points.title: Every distributor's sheet looks different
pain_points.detail: Claims arrive as spreadsheets, PDFs and photos in each distributor's own format, so the team re-keys before it can check anything.

pain_points.title: Scheme rules live in circulars
pain_points.detail: Validity dates, eligible SKUs, slabs and caps are scattered across circulars and emails, and different checkers apply them differently.

pain_points.title: Duplicates and ineligible lines
pain_points.detail: The same invoice claimed twice, claims under expired schemes or for ineligible SKUs, and inflated quantities slip through under volume.

pain_points.title: Settlement backlogs hurt the relationship
pain_points.detail: Slow settlement delays credit notes, and distributors hold payments or cut orders while they wait.

solution.overview: We build a claims platform that reads each distributor's claim sheet and supporting documents, normalises every line into a standard claim structure and matches it to secondary invoices, retailer acknowledgements and photo proofs. A scheme rule engine, configured from your circulars with validity dates, SKUs, slabs and caps, checks eligibility and recalculates the amount for each line. Duplicates are checked across months and distributors. Lines that pass go to a credit note sheet; uncertain or failed lines go to an exception queue with the reason and are never silently passed. Finance keeps final approval, and every decision is logged.
capabilities: Reads claim sheets, invoices, retailer acknowledgements and display photos in any distributor format
Scheme rule engine built from circulars, with validity dates, SKU lists, slabs, caps and version history
Recalculates the eligible amount for every claim line and shows it beside the claimed amount
Detects duplicate claims across months, schemes and distributors
Exception queue with reason codes for finance and trade marketing
Credit note sheet for finance approval and a line-by-line settlement statement for each distributor

workflow.title: Receive claims and proofs
workflow.detail: Distributors upload claim sheets and supporting documents through a portal or email, tagged by month and scheme.

workflow.title: Normalise claim lines
workflow.detail: Each line is extracted into a standard structure of distributor, scheme, invoice, SKU, quantity and claimed amount.

workflow.title: Match proofs
workflow.detail: Lines are matched to secondary invoices, acknowledgements and photos from the DMS and uploads.

workflow.title: Apply scheme rules and recalculate
workflow.detail: The rule engine checks eligibility, recalculates the amount and looks for duplicates.

workflow.title: Exception review
workflow.detail: Uncertain or failed lines go to finance or trade marketing with the reason and evidence.

workflow.title: Approve and settle
workflow.detail: Finance approves the credit note sheet, and distributors receive a line-by-line settlement statement.

inputs: Distributor claim sheets in Excel, CSV or PDF
Secondary sales invoices from the DMS
Retailer acknowledgements, display photos and damage or expiry notes
Scheme circulars with dates, SKUs, slabs and caps
Previous claims and settlements for duplicate checks
Finance mapping of claim types to ledgers
outputs: Normalised claim lines with recalculated eligible amounts
Exception list with reason codes and evidence
Credit note sheet for finance approval
Audit trail of every line decision
human_in_the_loop: Finance keeps final approval of every credit note sheet, and trade marketing rules on any scheme interpretation the rule engine cannot settle. Uncertain lines are always flagged for a person rather than passed.
integrations: Distributor management system for secondary sales
ERP such as SAP or Tally for credit notes
Shared drive or SharePoint for circulars
guardrails: No line approved without a matched proof
Scheme rules versioned with a reference to the source circular
Recalculated amount always shown beside the claimed amount
Duplicates blocked until a reviewer clears them
Input formats agreed and frozen before go-live
compliance_notes: The GST treatment of scheme discounts and credit notes depends on how schemes are agreed and documented; the system keeps the links between circular, invoice and credit note that your tax team needs.
A complete audit trail supports statutory audit of trade spends.

pilot.scope: One claim type, such as quantity-slab schemes, for the distributors of one region, using one month of finance-settled claims as the benchmark.
deliverables: Rule configuration for the pilot schemes
Working claims pipeline and exception queue
Credit note sheet in your finance format
Roll-out plan for other claim types and regions

what_we_measure.how: Line-level approve, reject and amount results compared with finance's settled claims.
Flags raised by the system and confirmed by finance.
Lines routed to the exception queue, by reason code.
Time from claim receipt to an approved credit note sheet, compared with the current process.

faqs.q: Our schemes change every month. How are rules kept up to date?
faqs.a: Trade marketing or the claims team enters each new circular into the rule register with its dates, SKUs and slabs, and the engine applies the version valid for the claim period. Ambiguous circulars are flagged for clarification instead of guessed.

faqs.q: Will distributors need to change their claim format?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The system reads varied formats, though agreeing a standard template over time reduces exceptions. We freeze the formats used in the pilot before sign-off.

faqs.q: Can it check display claim photos?
faqs.a: It checks that a photo exists, matches the retailer and period, and is not reused from another claim. Judging whether the display met the agreed standard can be added with shelf recognition.
